mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines relative to 12-month MA, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% and rises by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months, it signals labor market deterioration that increases probability of Fed rate cuts, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0% and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0% and rises >0.3pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900k and increase in residential credit (RSAFS) above 425k signals contraction in household demand and credit availability, indicating economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 900.0 and RSAFS > 425000.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals manufacturing weakness that increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 100.0 during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation requiring restrictive monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in less than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average indicates labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where PAYEMS > 12-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery, a rise in residential sales (RSAFS) above its 6-month moving average signals household consumption rebound, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS > 6-month MA during post-recession recovery, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 99.0 and increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.8% signals broad economic slowdown across manufacturing and labor markets, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 99.0 and UNRATE > 7.8%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.
